modules.title: Dimensions and unit
modules.doc:
A unit in physics arises from choice of something in physics which is non-canonical.
An example is the choice of translationally-invariant metric on the time manifold `TimeMan`.

A dimension is a property of a quantity related to how it changes with respect to a
change in the unit.

The fundamental choices one has in physics are related to:
- Time
- Length
- Mass
- Charge
- Temperature

(In fact temperature is not really a fundamental choice, however we leave this as a `TODO`.)

From these fundamental choices one can construct all other units and dimensions.

## Implementation details

Units within Physlib are implemented with the following convention:
- The fundamental units, and the choices they correspond to, are defined within the
  appropriate physics directory, in particular:
  - `Physlib/SpaceAndTime/Time/TimeUnit.lean`
  - `Physlib/SpaceAndTime/Space/LengthUnit.lean`
  - `Physlib/ClassicalMechanics/Mass/MassUnit.lean`
  - `Physlib/Electromagnetism/Charge/ChargeUnit.lean`
  - `Physlib/Thermodynamics/Temperature/TemperatureUnit.lean`
- In this `Units` directory, we define the necessary structures and properties
  to work derived units and dimensions.

## References

Zulip chats discussing units:

* https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/479953-Physlib/topic/physical.20units.
* https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/116395-maths/topic/Dimensional.20Analysis.20Revisited/with/530238303.

## Note

A lot of the results around units is still experimental and should be adapted based on needs.

## Other implementations of units

There are other implementations of units in Lean, in particular:
1. https://github.com/ATOMSLab/LeanDimensionalAnalysis/tree/main
2. https://github.com/teorth/analysis/blob/main/analysis/Analysis/Misc/SI.lean
3. https://github.com/ecyrbe/lean-units
Each of these have their own advantages and specific use-cases.
For example both (1) and (3) allow for or work in Floats, allowing computability and the use
of `#eval`. This is currently not possible with the more theoretical implementation here
in Physlib which is based exclusively on Reals.

sections.text:
## Types carrying dimensions

Dimensions are assigned to types with the following type-classes

- `HasDim` for any type `M` with an associated dimension
- `CarriesDimension` for a type that also has an instance of `MulAction ℝ≥0ˣ M`, that is an
  action of the strictly positive reals

Changing units rescales a quantity by a strictly positive factor: a length in metres is the same
length in feet times `0.3048`, and no change of units ever scales by zero. The strictly positive
reals `ℝ≥0ˣ` are therefore the natural scalars here, and `LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScaleUnits` records
the factor. Taking them rather than `ℝ≥0` is what lets a type whose elements are strictly
positive, such as `SpeedOfLight`, carry a dimension: on such a type a scaling compatible with
the magnitude, that is one satisfying `val (a • x) = a * val x`, cannot exist at `a = 0`, since
`val` is strictly positive.

A type with an action of `ℝ≥0`, such as `ℝ` or any real vector space, obtains the action of
`ℝ≥0ˣ` by restriction, and so carries a dimension as soon as it has a `HasDim` instance. A
declaration about such types should assume `[HasDim M]` and `[MulAction ℝ≥0 M]`, never
`[CarriesDimension M]` and `[MulAction ℝ≥0 M]` together: the latter pair puts two unrelated
actions of `ℝ≥0ˣ` in scope and proofs about the scaling get stuck. Where both actions genuinely
coexist, as on `Dimensionful M` below, the declared one and the one restricted from `ℝ≥0` agree
definitionally.

Several statements below therefore come in two forms: the plain name carries the `ℝ≥0` statement,
which the concrete unit calculations use, and the suffix `_units` the `ℝ≥0ˣ` statement, which
holds for every type carrying a dimension.

## Terms of the current dimension

Given a type `M` which carries a dimension `d`,
we are interested in elements of `M` which depend on a choice of units, i.e. functions
`LTMCTUnitChoices → M`.

We define both a proposition
- `HasDimension f` which says that `f` scales correctly with units,
and a type
- `Dimensionful M` which is the subtype of functions which `HasDimension`.

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices
declarations.doc: The choice of units.
declarations.statement:
structure LTMCTUnitChoices where
  /-- The length unit. -/
  length : LengthUnit
  /-- The time unit. -/
  time : TimeUnit
  /-- The mass unit. -/
  mass : MassUnit
  /-- The charge unit. -/
  charge : ChargeUnit
  /-- The temperature unit. -/
  temperature : TemperatureUnit

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale
declarations.doc:
Given two choices of units `u1` and `u2` and a dimension `d`, the
element of `ℝ≥0` corresponding to the scaling (by definition) of a quantity of dimension `d`
when changing from units `u1` to `u2`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def dimScale (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) :Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase →* ℝ≥0

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScale_apply (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    dimScale u1 u2 d =
      (u1.length / u2.length) ^ (d.length : ℝ) *
      (u1.time / u2.time) ^ (d.time : ℝ) *
      (u1.mass / u2.mass) ^ (d.mass : ℝ) *
      (u1.charge / u2.charge) ^ (d.charge : ℝ) *
      (u1.temperature / u2.temperature) ^ (d.temperature : ℝ)

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_self
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScale_self (u : LTMCTUnitChoices) (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    dimScale u u d = 1

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_one
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScale_one (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) :
    dimScale u1 u2 1 = 1

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_L𝓭
declarations.doc: The scale factor of the dimension of length is the ratio of the length units.
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScale_L𝓭 (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) :
    dimScale u1 u2 Dimension.L𝓭 = u1.length / u2.length

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_T𝓭
declarations.doc: The scale factor of the dimension of time is the ratio of the time units.
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScale_T𝓭 (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) :
    dimScale u1 u2 Dimension.T𝓭 = u1.time / u2.time

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_M𝓭
declarations.doc: The scale factor of the dimension of mass is the ratio of the mass units.
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScale_M𝓭 (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) :
    dimScale u1 u2 Dimension.M𝓭 = u1.mass / u2.mass

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_Θ𝓭
declarations.doc: The scale factor of the dimension of temperature is the ratio of the temperature units.
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScale_Θ𝓭 (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) :
    dimScale u1 u2 Dimension.Θ𝓭 = u1.temperature / u2.temperature

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_transitive
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScale_transitive (u1 u2 u3 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    dimScale u1 u2 d * dimScale u2 u3 d = dimScale u1 u3 d

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_mul_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScale_mul_symm (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    dimScale u1 u2 d * dimScale u2 u1 d = 1

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_coe_mul_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScale_coe_mul_symm (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    (toReal (dimScale u1 u2 d)) * (toReal (dimScale u2 u1 d)) = 1

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_ne_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScale_ne_zero (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    dimScale u1 u2 d ≠ 0

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScale_symm (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    dimScale u1 u2 d = (dimScale u2 u1 d)⁻¹

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_of_inv_eq_swap
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScale_of_inv_eq_swap (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    dimScale u1 u2 d⁻¹ = dimScale u2 u1 d

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.smul_dimScale_injective
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_dimScale_injective {M : Type} [MulAction ℝ≥0 M] (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices)
    (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) (m1 m2 : M) :
    (u1.dimScale u2 d) • m1 = (u1.dimScale u2 d) • m2 ↔ m1 = m2

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_pos
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScale_pos (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    0 < (dimScale u1 u2 d)

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScaleUnits
declarations.doc:
The scaling factor `dimScale u1 u2 d` regarded as a unit of `ℝ≥0`, that is as a strictly
positive real. Dimensionful quantities are scaled by this rather than by `dimScale u1 u2 d`
itself, so that a type whose elements are strictly positive, such as `SpeedOfLight`, can carry
a dimension: no action of `ℝ≥0` on such a type can be compatible with the magnitude, since
compatibility at `a = 0` would give `val (0 • m) = 0` while `val` is strictly positive.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dimScaleUnits (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    ℝ≥0ˣ

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScaleUnits_coe
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScaleUnits_coe (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    ((dimScaleUnits u1 u2 d : ℝ≥0)) = dimScale u1 u2 d

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScaleUnits_transitive
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScaleUnits_transitive (u1 u2 u3 : LTMCTUnitChoices)
    (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    dimScaleUnits u1 u2 d * dimScaleUnits u2 u3 d = dimScaleUnits u1 u3 d

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScaleUnits_smul
declarations.doc:
Scaling by `dimScaleUnits` agrees with scaling by `dimScale` whenever the type also carries
an action of `ℝ≥0`, so that statements phrased either way normalise to the same form.
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScaleUnits_smul {M : Type} [MulAction ℝ≥0 M] (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices)
    (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) (m : M) :
    dimScaleUnits u1 u2 d • m = dimScale u1 u2 d • m

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScaleUnits_mul_dim
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScaleUnits_mul_dim (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices)
    (d1 d2 : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    dimScaleUnits u1 u2 (d1 * d2) = dimScaleUnits u1 u2 d1 * dimScaleUnits u1 u2 d2

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScaleUnits_self
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScaleUnits_self (u : LTMCTUnitChoices) (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    dimScaleUnits u u d = 1

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.SI
declarations.doc:
The choice of units corresponding to SI units, that is
- meters,
- seconds,
- kilograms,
- coulombs,
- kelvin.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def SI : LTMCTUnitChoices

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.SI_length
declarations.statement: lemma SI_length : SI.length = LengthUnit.meters

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.SI_time
declarations.statement: lemma SI_time : SI.time = TimeUnit.seconds

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.SI_mass
declarations.statement: lemma SI_mass : SI.mass = MassUnit.kilograms

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.SI_charge
declarations.statement: lemma SI_charge : SI.charge = ChargeUnit.coulombs

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.SI_temperature
declarations.statement: lemma SI_temperature : SI.temperature = TemperatureUnit.kelvin

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.SIPrimed
declarations.doc:
A `LTMCTUnitChoices` which is related to `SI` by a prime scaling of each
of the underlying units. This is useful in proving that a result is not
dimensionally correct.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def SIPrimed : LTMCTUnitChoices

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_SI_SIPrimed
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScale_SI_SIPrimed (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    dimScale SI SIPrimed d =
      (2⁻¹ : ℝ≥0) ^ (d.length : ℝ) *
      (3⁻¹ : ℝ≥0) ^ (d.time : ℝ) *
      (5⁻¹ : ℝ≥0) ^ (d.mass : ℝ) *
      (7⁻¹ : ℝ≥0) ^ (d.charge : ℝ) *
      (11⁻¹ : ℝ≥0) ^ (d.temperature : ℝ)

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_SIPrimed_SI
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScale_SIPrimed_SI (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    dimScale SIPrimed SI d =
      (2 : ℝ≥0) ^ (d.length : ℝ) *
      (3 : ℝ≥0) ^ (d.time : ℝ) *
      (5 : ℝ≥0) ^ (d.mass : ℝ) *
      (7 : ℝ≥0) ^ (d.charge : ℝ) *
      (11 : ℝ≥0) ^ (d.temperature : ℝ)

declarations.name: HasDim
declarations.doc:
This typeclass indicates that there is a dimension `dim M : Dimension`
associated with the type `M`.
declarations.statement:
class HasDim (M : Type) where
  /-- The dimension associated with a type `M`. -/
  d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase

declarations.name: dim
declarations.statement: alias dim

declarations.name: abbrev
declarations.doc:
A type `M` carries a dimension `d` if every element of `M` is supposed to have
this dimension. For example, the type `Time` will carry a dimension `T𝓭`.
declarations.statement: class abbrev CarriesDimension (M : Type) := HasDim M, MulAction ℝ≥0ˣ M

declarations.name: HasDimension
declarations.doc:
A quantity of type `M` which depends on a choice of units `LTMCTUnitChoices` is said to be
of dimension `d` if it scales by `LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScaleUnits u1 u2 d` under a change in
units.
declarations.statement: def HasDimension {M : Type} [CarriesDimension M] (f : LTMCTUnitChoices → M) : Prop

declarations.name: hasDimension_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDimension_iff {M : Type} [CarriesDimension M] (f : LTMCTUnitChoices → M) :
    HasDimension f ↔ ∀ u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices, f u2 =
    LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScaleUnits u1 u2 (dim M) • f u1

declarations.name: Dimensionful
declarations.doc:
The subtype of functions `LTMCTUnitChoices → M`, for which `M` carries a dimension,
which `HasDimension`.
declarations.statement: def Dimensionful (M : Type) [CarriesDimension M]

instance {M : Type} [CarriesDimension M] :
    CoeFun (Dimensionful M) (fun _ => LTMCTUnitChoices → M)

declarations.name: Dimensionful.ext
declarations.statement:
lemma Dimensionful.ext {M : Type} [CarriesDimension M] (f1 f2 : Dimensionful M)
    (h : f1.val = f2.val) : f1 = f2
instance {M : Type} [CarriesDimension M] : MulAction ℝ≥0ˣ (Dimensionful M)

declarations.doc:
When `M` itself carries an action of `ℝ≥0`, a dimensionful quantity of `M` may be scaled by
any non-negative real, not only by a strictly positive one.
declarations.statement:
instance {M : Type} [HasDim M] [MulAction ℝ≥0 M] :
    MulAction ℝ≥0 (Dimensionful M)

declarations.name: Dimensionful.smul_apply
declarations.doc: The value of a non-negative real scaling of a dimensionful quantity.
declarations.statement:
lemma Dimensionful.smul_apply {M : Type} [HasDim M] [MulAction ℝ≥0 M]
    (a : ℝ≥0) (f : Dimensionful M) (u : LTMCTUnitChoices) :
    (a • f).1 u = a • f.1 u

declarations.name: Dimensionful.smul_apply_units
declarations.statement:
lemma Dimensionful.smul_apply_units {M : Type} [CarriesDimension M]
    (a : ℝ≥0ˣ) (f : Dimensionful M) (u : LTMCTUnitChoices) :
    (a • f).1 u = a • f.1 u

declarations.name: CarriesDimension.toDimensionful
declarations.doc:
For `M` carrying a dimension `d`, the equivalence between `M` and `Dimension M`,
given a choice of units.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def CarriesDimension.toDimensionful {M : Type} [CarriesDimension M]
    (u : LTMCTUnitChoices) :
    M ≃ Dimensionful M

declarations.name: CarriesDimension.toDimensionful_apply_apply_units
declarations.doc:
The value of `toDimensionful`, scaled by `dimScaleUnits`. This is the general form, holding
for every type carrying a dimension.
declarations.statement:
lemma CarriesDimension.toDimensionful_apply_apply_units
    {M : Type} [CarriesDimension M] (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (m : M) :
    (toDimensionful u1 m).1 u2 = (u1.dimScaleUnits u2 (dim M)) • m

declarations.name: CarriesDimension.toDimensionful_apply_apply
declarations.doc:
The value of `toDimensionful` for a type which also carries an action of `ℝ≥0`, phrased with
`dimScale` in place of `dimScaleUnits`. This is the form the concrete unit calculations use.
declarations.statement:
lemma CarriesDimension.toDimensionful_apply_apply
    {M : Type} [HasDim M] [MulAction ℝ≥0 M] (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (m : M) :
    (toDimensionful u1 m).1 u2 = (u1.dimScale u2 (dim M)) • m

declarations.name: CarriesDimension.toDimensionful_apply_self
declarations.doc:
Reading a quantity built by `toDimensionful u` back in the same unit choice `u` returns the
value it was built from.
declarations.statement:
lemma CarriesDimension.toDimensionful_apply_self
    {M : Type} [CarriesDimension M] (u : LTMCTUnitChoices) (m : M) :
    toDimensionful u m u = m

modules.title: Physical constants
modules.doc:
An index of the physical constants in Physlib, and the format of their files.

## i. Overview

Each constant has its own file, which this module imports. Use these constants instead of defining
new ones or writing out their values: a result in any units takes the type, such as
`c : SpeedOfLight`, and the value in our world is `speedOfLight`. A new constant gets a file in the
format of section A, an import above, a row in the table below and an `example` in section B.

## ii. Key results

| Constant | Dimension | Value in SI units |
|---|---|---|
| `speedOfLight` | `L T⁻¹` | `299792458 m s⁻¹`, exact |
| `boltzmannConstant` | `M L² T⁻² Θ⁻¹` | `1.380649 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹`, exact |

Not yet in this format: `Constants.h`, `Constants.ℏ` and `ChargeUnit.elementaryCharge`.

- `exists_units_constants_eq_one` : There are units in which the speed of light and the Boltzmann
  constant are `1`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The format of a constant
- B. Checked values
- C. Planck units

## iv. References

* The defining constants of the SI. [ref: bipm_si_brochure_2019]

## A. The format of a constant

The file of a constant with type `X` and value `x` has these sections, as in
`Physlib/Relativity/SpeedOfLight.lean`.

| Section | Contents |
|---|---|
| A. The type | `structure X` with fields `val : ℝ` and `pos : 0 < val` |
| B. Instances | `X.instPositiveRealUnitCore`, `Coe X ℝ`, `X.positiveRealUnitCore_val` |
| C. Positivity | `X.val_pos`, `X.val_nonneg`, `X.val_ne_zero` |
| D. The dimension | `X.instHasDim` |
| E. The value in our world | `x : Dimensionful X` and `x_in_SI` |
| F. Specific to this constant | Optional, for example `One` or other forms of the constant |

The value `x` is `X` in lower camel case, defined by `toDimensionful SI`, and `x_in_SI` is proved by
`toDimensionful_apply_self`. The docstring of `x` gives the number with its SI unit, followed by
`exact` or, for a measured constant, the CODATA edition.

sections.text:
## B. Checked values

One `example` for each row of the table, giving the dimension and the value in SI units. Lean
checks these against the definitions; it does not read the table.

## C. Planck units

Planck units are units in which `c`, `ℏ`, `G` and `k_B` are all `1`; so far the lemma below covers
`c` and `k_B`. Constants with independent dimensions can always be `1` together, while constants
with dependent dimensions can only if their dimensionless ratios are `1`. So the lemma does not
extend to every constant: `h` cannot join `ℏ`, and the electron mass cannot join `c`, `ℏ` and `G`.

declarations.name: exists_units_constants_eq_one
declarations.doc: There are units in which the speed of light and the Boltzmann constant are `1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_units_constants_eq_one : ∃ u : LTMCTUnitChoices,
    (speedOfLight u).val = 1 ∧ (boltzmannConstant u).val = 1

modules.title: Dimension
modules.doc:
In this module we define the type `Dimension` which carries the dimension
of a physical quantity.

A `Dimension B` is parameterised by a *basis* `B` of base dimensions equipped with a
`DimensionBasis` representation. Each representation is additively equivalent to assigning an
`Exponent` to every base dimension `b : B`. The parameterisation is purely in
the dimensional *algebra*: `Dimension B` is a `CommGroup` for every represented basis `B`
(multiplication adds exponents, inversion negates them), so quantities can be typed by
dimensions over any basis. The commutative-group, `Exponent`- and `ℚ`-power structures, decidable
equality (`DecidableEq`), the base vectors `single b`, and the change-of-basis map
`extend` are all generic in `B`.

PhysLib's default basis is `LTMCTDimensionBase` — length, time, mass, charge,
temperature — whose projections and named generators (`L𝓭`, `T𝓭`, …) live in
`Physlib.Units.LTMCTDimensionBase`. It is *charge*-based with five generators, so it
is **not** the SI/ISQ base-quantity set; the ISQ set is `ISQDimensionBase`, and other
systems (Gaussian–CGS, natural units, …) are equally expressible as `Dimension B` for
a suitable basis `B`.

sections.text:
## Dimension-preserving maps between bases

A cross-basis map of dimensions is only admissible if it preserves the dimensional
*algebra*. We record the two truth-preserving directions as bundled data:

* an `Embedding B B'` is an **injective** `MonoidHom (Dimension B) (Dimension B')` — a
  faithful, dimension-preserving inclusion of one basis into another; and
* a `Projection B' B` is a **surjective** `MonoidHom (Dimension B') (Dimension B)` — a
  truth-preserving *reduction* of a richer basis onto a coarser one.

Being a `MonoidHom` is what makes either map dimension-preserving (it respects
products, inverses and rational powers); the injectivity / surjectivity side condition
distinguishes the two directions. Cross-basis dimension maps should be produced as one
of these, so that dimension-preservation holds by construction — a bare relabelling
that sends a base dimension to an inequivalent one is *not* expressible as either.

declarations.name: DimensionBasis
declarations.doc:
A choice of exponent-tuple representation for a basis `B`. Native addition on `Exponents`
is used for dimension multiplication, while `exponentEquiv` provides the basis-generic API.
declarations.statement:
class DimensionBasis (B : Type) where
  /-- The native tuple of exponents for this basis. -/
  Exponents : Type
  /-- The additive structure on native exponent tuples. -/
  [addCommGroup : AddCommGroup Exponents]
  /-- Native exponent tuples are additively equivalent to exponent functions on the basis. -/
  exponentEquiv : Exponents ≃+ (B → Dimension.Exponent)

declarations.name: DimensionBasis.pi
declarations.doc: The function-backed exponent representation for a basis without a specialized tuple.
declarations.statement: def pi (B : Type) : DimensionBasis B

declarations.name: Dimension
declarations.doc:
A dimension over a represented basis `B`. PhysLib's default basis is
`LTMCTDimensionBase`.
declarations.statement:
structure Dimension (B : Type) [DimensionBasis B] where
  /-- The dimension's native exponent tuple. -/
  exponents : DimensionBasis.Exponents B

declarations.name: Dimension.exponent
declarations.doc: The exponent of a dimension at a base dimension.
declarations.statement: def exponent (d : Dimension B) : B → Exponent

declarations.name: Dimension.ofFunction
declarations.doc: Construct a dimension from an exponent function.
declarations.statement: def ofFunction (f : B → Exponent) : Dimension B

declarations.name: Dimension.ofFunction_exponent
declarations.statement: lemma ofFunction_exponent (f : B → Exponent) (b : B) : (ofFunction f).exponent b = f b

declarations.name: Dimension.ext

declarations.name: Dimension.extend
declarations.doc:
Change of basis along a map `f : B → B'` of base dimensions: reindex a dimension
over `B` into one over `B'` by placing each exponent at its image. For an embedding
`f` (injective) this preserves every exponent (`extend_exponent_apply`), so a
dimension in one system re-expresses faithfully in an extending one.
declarations.statement:
def extend {B' : Type} [DimensionBasis B'] [Fintype B] [DecidableEq B']
    (f : B → B') (d : Dimension B) : Dimension B'

declarations.name: Dimension.extend_exponent_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma extend_exponent_apply {B' : Type} [DimensionBasis B'] [Fintype B] [DecidableEq B']
    {f : B → B'} (hf : Function.Injective f) (d : Dimension B) (b : B) :
    (extend f d).exponent (f b) = d.exponent b

declarations.name: Dimension.extendHom
declarations.doc: `extend f` packaged as a monoid homomorphism of dimensions.
declarations.statement:
def extendHom {B' : Type} [DimensionBasis B'] [Fintype B] [DecidableEq B'] (f : B → B') :
    Dimension B →* Dimension B'

declarations.name: Dimension.Embedding
declarations.doc:
A **dimension embedding** `B ↪ B'`: an injective monoid homomorphism of
dimensions. As a `MonoidHom` it is dimension-preserving (it respects products,
inverses and rational powers); injectivity makes it a faithful inclusion of the basis
`B` into `B'`. Cross-basis dimension injections are produced as `Embedding`s so that
dimension-preservation holds by construction.
declarations.statement:
structure Embedding (B B' : Type) [DimensionBasis B] [DimensionBasis B'] where
  /-- The underlying dimension-preserving homomorphism. -/
  toHom : Dimension B →* Dimension B'
  /-- The homomorphism is injective (a faithful embedding). -/
  inj : Function.Injective toHom

declarations.name: Dimension.Projection
declarations.doc:
A **dimension projection** `B' ↠ B`: a surjective monoid homomorphism of
dimensions. As a `MonoidHom` it is truth-preserving, but it is lossy — it reduces a
richer basis `B'` onto a coarser basis `B`, collapsing the base dimensions that `B`
does not track.
declarations.statement:
structure Projection (B' B : Type) [DimensionBasis B'] [DimensionBasis B] where
  /-- The underlying dimension-preserving homomorphism. -/
  toHom : Dimension B' →* Dimension B
  /-- The homomorphism is surjective (the reduction hits every dimension of `B`). -/
  surj : Function.Surjective toHom

declarations.name: Dimension.Embedding.ofBasis
declarations.doc:
An injective *basis* map `f : B → B'` induces a dimension embedding, via `extend`.
This is the label-level case: it sends each base dimension of `B` to a base dimension
of `B'`, so it is automatically dimension-preserving and faithful.
declarations.statement:
def Embedding.ofBasis {B B' : Type} [DimensionBasis B] [DimensionBasis B']
    [Fintype B] [DecidableEq B']
    (f : B → B') (hf : Function.Injective f) : Embedding B B'

modules.title: Reducible rational arithmetic for dimension exponents
modules.doc:
This module defines `Exponent`, a wrapper around the rational numbers whose arithmetic is
reducible. This lets concrete arithmetic on dimension exponents hold by definitional equality.

The corresponding rational operations are irreducible in Lean. Locally unsealing them does not
export their reducibility to downstream modules, while globally changing the reducibility of an
imported declaration requires `allowUnsafeReducibility`. The wrapper instead owns transparent
operations while remaining equivalent to `ℚ`.

The reducibility guarantee applies to the custom addition, subtraction, multiplication, inversion,
and division below. Other operations supplied by the `Field` instance are transferred from `ℚ`.
In particular, rational scalar multiplication and negative integer powers may require propositional
reasoning rather than `rfl`.

modules.title: Dimensional invariance of fderiv
modules.doc:
In this module we prove that the derivative is dimensionally correct.
That is to say for a function `f : M1 → M2` where `M1` carries dimensions `d1` and `M2` carries
dimension `d2` such that `f` has the correct dimension, then
`fderiv ℝ f : M1 → M1 →L[ℝ] M2` has the correct dimensions.

To give an explicit example let us say `M1` has dimension `L𝓭` and `M2` has dimension
`L𝓭 * L𝓭` and `f : M1 → M2 : x ↦ x ^ 2`, this is dimensionally correct.
The `fderiv` of this `fderiv ℝ f : M1 → M1 →L[ℝ] M2` takes
`x dx ↦ dx • (2 * x)` which is still dimensionally correct. Here `dx` is the direction
in which the derivative is taken.

declarations.name: fderiv_apply_scaleUnit
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_apply_scaleUnit (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (x dm : M1)
    (f : M1 → M2) (hf : IsDimensionallyCorrect f) (f_diff : Differentiable ℝ f) :
    fderiv ℝ f (scaleUnit u2 u1 x) dm =
    u2.dimScale u1 (dim M2) • u1.dimScale u2 (dim M1) • fderiv ℝ f x dm

declarations.name: fderiv_isDimensionallyCorrect
declarations.doc: If a function is dimensionally valid then so is it's derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_isDimensionallyCorrect (f : M1 → M2) (hf : IsDimensionallyCorrect f)
    (f_diff : Differentiable ℝ f) :
    IsDimensionallyCorrect (fderiv ℝ f)

declarations.name: fderiv_dimension_const_direction
declarations.doc:
The expression `fderiv ℝ f x dm = v.1` for a fixed `dm` and for
`v` with dimension `d M2 * (d M1)⁻¹` is dimensionally correct. This is the
ordinary manifestation of dimensions of a derivative, usually `dm` is taken as e.g. `1`.

This result also shows that dimensional correctness does depend on what
quantities are considered dimensionful.
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_dimension_const_direction (dm : M1) (f : M1 → M2) (hf : IsDimensionallyCorrect f)
    (f_diff : Differentiable ℝ f) :
    IsDimensionallyCorrect (fun x (v : WithDim (dim M2 * (dim M1)⁻¹) M2) =>
      fderiv ℝ f x dm = v.1)

modules.title: Bridging PhysLib's default basis and the ISQ basis
modules.doc:
`LTMCTDimensionBase` (length, time, mass, charge, temperature) and `ISQDimensionBase`
(the seven ISO/IEC 80000-1 base quantities) make different base/derived choices. This
module relates them by the two truth-preserving directions of `Dimension.Embedding`
and `Dimension.Projection`:

* `ltmctToISQ : Dimension.Embedding LTMCTDimensionBase ISQDimensionBase` — the
  dimension-preserving **inclusion** of PhysLib dimensions into ISQ dimensions. It
  sends the charge generator to the *derived* ISQ charge `I · T` (`toISQHom_C𝓭`), so it
  is faithful (`toISQHom_injective`) and physically correct, not a bare relabelling.
* `isqToLTMCT : Dimension.Projection ISQDimensionBase LTMCTDimensionBase` — the
  truth-preserving **reduction** of ISQ dimensions onto PhysLib's. It reads electric
  current as charge/time and forgets amount of substance and luminous intensity (the
  base quantities PhysLib does not track).

The two fit together as a retraction, `isqToLTMCT ∘ ltmctToISQ = id`
(`isqToLTMCT_comp_ltmctToISQ`): PhysLib's basis embeds faithfully into ISQ and is
recovered exactly by the projection — but the reverse composite is *not* the identity,
because amount of substance and luminous intensity cannot be recovered once dropped.
That is the asymmetry: one can reduce ISQ to LTMCT, but not conjure the extra base
quantities back without *adding* them.

declarations.name: Dimension.toISQFun
declarations.doc:
The function underlying `toISQHom`: fix length, mass, time and temperature, and
send PhysLib's charge generator to the derived ISQ charge `I · T` (the current

modules.title: The ISQ base quantities
modules.doc:
The International System of Quantities (ISQ), specified in ISO/IEC 80000-1 and
described in the International Vocabulary of Metrology (VIM, 3rd edition,
JCGM 200:2012), fixes seven mutually independent *base quantities*: length, mass,
time, electric current, thermodynamic temperature, amount of substance, and
luminous intensity.

`ISQDimensionBase` is that seven-element basis, realised as an instantiation
`Dimension ISQDimensionBase` of the parametric dimensional algebra. It differs from
PhysLib's default `LTMCTDimensionBase` in two ways:

* the electromagnetic base quantity is *electric current*, so electric charge is a
  *derived* dimension (`Q = I · T`, `ISQDimensionBase.charge`); and
* *amount of substance* and *luminous intensity* are additional independent base
  quantities.

## References

* ISO/IEC 80000-1:2009, Quantities and units — Part 1: General. [ref: iso_80000_1_2009]
* JCGM 200:2012, International vocabulary of metrology — Basic and general concepts and associated
  terms (VIM, 3rd edition). [ref: jcgm_200_2012]

modules.title: PhysLib's default dimension basis
modules.doc:
`LTMCTDimensionBase` is PhysLib's default basis of base dimensions — length, time,
mass, charge and temperature. `Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase` is the familiar
five-exponent dimension, and this module provides the concrete API on top of the
generic `Dimension B`:

* the `.length`, `.time`, `.mass`, `.charge`, `.temperature` exponent projections;
* the `ofLTMCTDimensionBase` constructor from five exponents; and
* the named generators `L𝓭`, `T𝓭`, `M𝓭`, `C𝓭`, `Θ𝓭`, shown to be the generic
  `single` base vectors.

This basis is *charge*-based with five generators, so it is deliberately **not** the
SI/ISQ base-quantity set (which takes electric current as base and adds amount of
substance and luminous intensity); see `ISQDimensionBase`.

## The named generators are the base vectors

Each named generator `L𝓭`, `T𝓭`, … is the generic `single` base vector at the
corresponding base dimension, exhibiting them as instances of the basis-generic API.

modules.title: Examples: parametric dimensions and comparing dimensioned quantities
modules.doc:
`Dimension B` is parameterised by a basis `B` of base dimensions. This module
illustrates two consequences.

## Comparing a length with a velocity times a time

A recurring question is how to compare a quantity of dimension `length` with a
product of a quantity of dimension `length / time` and a quantity of dimension
`time`. In the fixed-tuple representation of `LTMCTDimensionBase`, reducible exponent
arithmetic makes this concrete cancellation a definitional equality:

* `(L𝓭 / T𝓭) * T𝓭 = L𝓭` is closed by `rfl`.
* `WithDim ((L𝓭 / T𝓭) * T𝓭) ℝ` and `WithDim L𝓭 ℝ` are therefore definitionally
  equal types.

Consequently a bare `x = v * t` is well-typed for these concrete dimensions. For a
representation where the same cancellation holds only propositionally, `WithDim.cast`
bridges the two dimension-indexed types.

## A non-standard basis

Because `Dimension` is parametric, the same dimensional algebra and `cast`-based
comparison are available over any represented basis, not just the physical
`LTMCTDimensionBase`. The unit-scaling layer (`LTMCTUnitChoices`, `dimScale`) is not
needed for either the algebra or the comparison, so neither is referenced here.

This module is illustrative and should not be imported by other modules.

sections.text:
## The same comparison over a non-standard basis

A basis with two base dimensions of its own — `bit` and `symbol` — that
`LTMCTDimensionBase` does not have. Nothing in the standard units system is involved.

modules.title: The unit side, parametrised in the same basis
modules.doc:
The dimension basis is parametric (`Dimension B`), but the *unit* side of the
bridge is hardwired in parallel: `LTMCTUnitChoices` has five named unit fields and
`LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale` folds over exactly those five. This module provides the
generic twin, parametrised in the same basis `B`.

Every PhysLib base unit (`LengthUnit`, `TimeUnit`, …) is, structurally, a positive
real (`{ val : ℝ // 0 < val }`); the typed names carry no extra algebraic content.
So a unit choice over a basis `B` is a positive real per base dimension, and the
scaling homomorphism folds the per-base unit ratio over `B`:

* `UnitScale B` — a positive-real magnitude for each `b : B`.
* `UnitScale.dimScale : UnitScale B → UnitScale B → Dimension B →* ℝ≥0` — the
  `MonoidHom` `d ↦ ∏ b, (u₁ b / u₂ b) ^ d.exponent b`, generic in `B`.

The current five-field `LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale` is the `LTMCTDimensionBase` instance of this
fold, written out by hand; `LTMCTUnitChoices.toScale` exhibits the correspondence.

sections.text:
## The current five-field `LTMCTUnitChoices` is the `LTMCTDimensionBase` instance

`LTMCTUnitChoices.toScale` reads the five typed units as a `UnitScale LTMCTDimensionBase`,
exhibiting the existing bespoke `dimScale` as the `LTMCTDimensionBase` case of the generic
fold.

declarations.name: UnitScale
declarations.doc:
A choice of unit for each base dimension of `B`: a positive-real magnitude per
base. This is the basis-generic form of `LTMCTUnitChoices`.
declarations.statement:
structure UnitScale (B : Type) where
  /-- The positive-real magnitude of the chosen unit at each base dimension. -/
  scale : B → ℝ≥0
  /-- Each chosen unit has a positive magnitude. -/
  scale_pos : ∀ b, 0 < scale b

declarations.name: UnitScale.ratio_ne_zero
declarations.statement: lemma ratio_ne_zero (u1 u2 : UnitScale B) (b : B) : u1.scale b / u2.scale b ≠ 0

declarations.name: UnitScale.dimScale
declarations.doc:
The dimension-scaling homomorphism, generic in the basis `B`: a quantity of
dimension `d` rescales by `∏ b, (u1 b / u2 b) ^ d.exponent b` when changing the
unit choice from `u1` to `u2`. This is the basis-generic form of
`LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dimScale [DimensionBasis B] [Fintype B]
    (u1 u2 : UnitScale B) : Dimension B →* ℝ≥0

declarations.name: UnitScale.dimScale_self
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScale_self [DimensionBasis B] [Fintype B] (u : UnitScale B) (d : Dimension B) :
    dimScale u u d = 1

declarations.name: UnitScale.dimScale_one
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScale_one [DimensionBasis B] [Fintype B] (u1 u2 : UnitScale B) :
    dimScale u1 u2 1 = 1

declarations.name: UnitScale.dimScale_transitive
declarations.doc: The scaling is transitive (a cocycle in the unit choices).
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScale_transitive [DimensionBasis B] [Fintype B]
    (u1 u2 u3 : UnitScale B) (d : Dimension B) :
    dimScale u1 u2 d * dimScale u2 u3 d = dimScale u1 u3 d

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.toScale
declarations.doc: Read a five-field `LTMCTUnitChoices` as a `UnitScale` over `LTMCTDimensionBase`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def toScale (u : LTMCTUnitChoices) : UnitScale LTMCTDimensionBase

modules.title: A. Shared arithmetic for positive-real unit types
modules.doc:
`PositiveRealUnitCore` records a unit magnitude and its inverse construction.
Each concrete unit declares this instance explicitly and keeps its own structure.
The inhabited and same-type division instances, rescaling operation, and arithmetic
laws are provided generically. No command or type-specific lemma wrappers are needed.

The arithmetic is adapted from the existing unit modules by Joseph Tooby-Smith.
This interface describes an individual unit type, independently of the selection
and combination of units by `UnitMagnitudeCatalog` and `UnitSystem`.

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore
declarations.doc: Common representation API for unit types whose magnitude is a positive real.
declarations.statement:
class PositiveRealUnitCore (U : Type) where
  /-- The underlying real magnitude of a unit. -/
  val : U → ℝ
  /-- Every unit has a strictly positive magnitude. -/
  pos : ∀ x, 0 < val x
  /-- Construct a unit from a positive real magnitude. -/
  ofVal : (r : ℝ) → 0 < r → U
  /-- Construction preserves the supplied magnitude. -/
  val_ofVal : ∀ r hr, val (ofVal r hr) = r
  /-- Reconstructing a unit from its magnitude returns that unit. -/
  ofVal_val : ∀ x, ofVal (val x) (pos x) = x

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.instInhabited
declarations.doc: The unit of magnitude one supplies a default unit.
declarations.statement: instance (priority := 100) instInhabited : Inhabited U

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.val_ne_zero
declarations.statement: lemma val_ne_zero (x : U) : val x ≠ 0

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.ratio
declarations.doc: The ratio of the magnitudes of two units of the same type.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def ratio (x y : U) : NNReal

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.instHDiv
declarations.doc: Division of two units of the same type is their nonnegative real ratio.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance (priority := 100) instHDiv : HDiv U U NNReal

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.div_eq_val
declarations.doc: Unit division agrees with the ratio of the two magnitudes.
declarations.statement:
lemma div_eq_val (x y : U) :
    x / y = (⟨val x / val y, _root_.div_nonneg (pos x).le (pos y).le⟩ : NNReal)

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.div_pos
declarations.statement: lemma div_pos (x y : U) : (0 : NNReal) < x / y

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.div_ne_zero
declarations.statement: lemma div_ne_zero (x y : U) : x / y ≠ (0 : NNReal)

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.div_self
declarations.statement: lemma div_self (x : U) : x / x = (1 : NNReal)

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.div_symm
declarations.statement: lemma div_symm (x y : U) : x / y = (y / x : NNReal)⁻¹

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.div_mul_div
declarations.doc: Unit ratios compose along an intermediate choice of unit.
declarations.statement: lemma div_mul_div (x y z : U) : (x / y : NNReal) * (y / z) = x / z

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.div_mul_div_coe
declarations.statement:
lemma div_mul_div_coe (x y z : U) :
    (x / y : ℝ) * (y / z : ℝ) = x / z

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.scale
declarations.doc: Rescale a unit by a strictly positive real factor.
declarations.statement: def scale (r : ℝ) (x : U) (hr : 0 < r := by norm_num) : U

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.scale_val
declarations.statement:
lemma scale_val (r : ℝ) (x : U) (hr : 0 < r) :
    val (scale r x hr) = r * val x

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.ext
declarations.doc: Units with equal magnitudes are equal.
declarations.statement: lemma ext {x y : U} (h : val x = val y) : x = y

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.unitsSMul
declarations.doc:
The rescaling of a unit magnitude by a strictly positive real, given as a unit of `ℝ≥0`.
This is `scale` at a factor known to be positive, so the `scale` lemmas may be applied to
`u • x` after rewriting with `units_smul_eq_scale`.
declarations.statement: def unitsSMul (u : ℝ≥0ˣ) (x : U) : U

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.instMulActionUnitsNNReal
declarations.doc:
A unit magnitude may be rescaled by a strictly positive real, that is by a unit of `ℝ≥0`.
No action of `ℝ≥0` on `U` can be compatible with the magnitude: taking `a > 0` and `b = 0` in
`mul_smul` would force `0 • x` to be a fixed point of every rescaling, and no element of `U`
is.
declarations.statement: instance instMulActionUnitsNNReal : MulAction ℝ≥0ˣ U

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.units_smul_eq_scale
declarations.doc:
A rescaling by a unit of `ℝ≥0` is the rescaling by its underlying positive factor. Rewriting
with this makes the `scale` lemmas applicable; `simp` does not see through `HSMul.hSMul` on its
own.
declarations.statement:
lemma units_smul_eq_scale (u : ℝ≥0ˣ) (x : U) :
    u • x = scale ((u : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) x (by
      have hu : ((u : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by simp [Units.ne_zero u]
      exact lt_of_le_of_ne (by positivity) (Ne.symm hu))

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.val_units_smul
declarations.doc: The magnitude of a rescaling by a unit of `ℝ≥0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma val_units_smul (u : ℝ≥0ˣ) (x : U) :
    val (u • x) = ((u : ℝ≥0) : ℝ) * val x

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.scale_div_self
declarations.doc: The ratio of a rescaled unit to the original is the scaling factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma scale_div_self (x : U) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) :
    scale r x hr / x = (⟨r, le_of_lt hr⟩ : NNReal)

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.self_div_scale
declarations.doc: The reverse ratio is the reciprocal of the scaling factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma self_div_scale (x : U) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) :
    x / scale r x hr =
      (⟨1 / r, _root_.div_nonneg (by simp) (le_of_lt hr)⟩ : NNReal)

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.scale_one
declarations.statement: lemma scale_one (x : U) : scale 1 x = x

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.scale_div_scale
declarations.doc: Rescaling two units multiplies their ratio by the ratio of the factors.
declarations.statement:
lemma scale_div_scale (x1 x2 : U) {r1 r2 : ℝ} (hr1 : 0 < r1) (hr2 : 0 < r2) :
    scale r1 x1 hr1 / scale r2 x2 hr2 =
      (⟨r1, le_of_lt hr1⟩ / ⟨r2, le_of_lt hr2⟩ : NNReal) * (x1 / x2)

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.scale_scale
declarations.doc: Successive rescalings compose by multiplication of their factors.
declarations.statement:
lemma scale_scale (x : U) (r1 r2 : ℝ) (hr1 : 0 < r1) (hr2 : 0 < r2) :
    scale r1 (scale r2 x hr2) hr1 =
      scale (r1 * r2) x (mul_pos hr1 hr2)

declarations.name: PositiveRealUnitCore.scale_div
declarations.doc: Rescaling a unit by the ratio to a target unit produces that target.
declarations.statement:
lemma scale_div (x y : U) (hr : 0 < (y / x : ℝ)) :
    scale (y / x) x hr = y

modules.title: A typed unit choice over the ISQ base quantities (the SI units)
modules.doc:
`LTMCTUnitChoices` is the typed unit choice over PhysLib's default dimension basis
`LTMCTDimensionBase`. This module gives the *second* typed unit choice — over the
seven ISQ base quantities `ISQDimensionBase` — realised through the basis-generic
`UnitMagnitudeCatalog` / `UnitSystem` machinery of `Physlib.Units.UnitSystem`. It is the concrete
payoff of parametrising the unit side: the same generic layer produces a fully *typed*
unit choice over a different basis, and the scaling homomorphism comes for free from
`UnitScale.dimScale` — nothing is re-proved by hand.

The ISQ base quantities are length, mass, time, electric current, thermodynamic
temperature, amount of substance and luminous intensity. Four of the corresponding typed
unit types already exist (`LengthUnit`, `MassUnit`, `TimeUnit`, `TemperatureUnit`); the
remaining three — `CurrentUnit`, `AmountUnit`, `LuminousIntensityUnit` — are introduced
here. They follow the `LengthUnit` convention of a positive-real magnitude and support
rescaling and unit-ratio laws through `PositiveRealUnitCore`. Following PhysLib's
layout, these types may ultimately live under the relevant physics directories.

`SIUnitChoices := UnitSystem ISQDimensionBase` is then the typed SI unit choice, and
`SIUnitChoices.SI` is the coherent SI choice (metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin,
mole, candela). Contrast `SIUnitChoices` (current-based, seven typed slots) with
`LTMCTUnitChoices` (charge-based, five typed slots): the machinery supports both, and the
`Dimension.ltmctToISQ` / `Dimension.isqToLTMCT` bridge relates their bases.

sections.text: ## Typed unit types for the ISQ base quantities not already present

## The ISQ `UnitMagnitudeCatalog` instance

Each ISQ base quantity is assigned its typed unit type; the magnitude layer is the
positive-real `val`, exactly as for the `LTMCTDimensionBase` instance.
## Folding over the ISQ base quantities

declarations.name: CurrentUnit
declarations.doc:
A unit of electric current — a choice of positive-real magnitude. The SI coherent
choice is the ampere.
declarations.statement:
structure CurrentUnit where
  /-- The underlying scale of the unit. -/
  val : ℝ
  property : 0 < val
instance : PositiveRealUnitCore CurrentUnit

declarations.name: CurrentUnit.amperes
declarations.doc: The SI coherent unit of electric current, the ampere.
declarations.statement: def amperes : CurrentUnit

declarations.name: CurrentUnit.milliamperes
declarations.doc: One milliampere, equal to `10⁻³` amperes.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def milliamperes : CurrentUnit

declarations.name: AmountUnit
declarations.doc:
A unit of amount of substance — a choice of positive-real magnitude. The SI coherent
choice is the mole.
declarations.statement:
structure AmountUnit where
  /-- The underlying scale of the unit. -/
  val : ℝ
  property : 0 < val
instance : PositiveRealUnitCore AmountUnit

declarations.name: AmountUnit.moles
declarations.doc: The SI coherent unit of amount of substance, the mole.
declarations.statement: def moles : AmountUnit

declarations.name: LuminousIntensityUnit
declarations.doc:
A unit of luminous intensity — a choice of positive-real magnitude. The SI coherent
choice is the candela.
declarations.statement:
structure LuminousIntensityUnit where
  /-- The underlying scale of the unit. -/
  val : ℝ
  property : 0 < val
instance : PositiveRealUnitCore LuminousIntensityUnit

declarations.name: LuminousIntensityUnit.candelas
declarations.doc: The SI coherent unit of luminous intensity, the candela.
declarations.statement: def candelas : LuminousIntensityUnit
noncomputable instance : UnitMagnitudeCatalog ISQDimensionBase

declarations.name: prod_univ_ISQDimensionBase
declarations.doc:
The product over the seven ISQ base quantities, in canonical enumeration order — the
`ISQDimensionBase` companion to `prod_univ_LTMCTDimensionBase`, a reusable fact about the
`Fintype` enumeration for folding `Finset.prod` over the ISQ basis.
declarations.statement:
lemma prod_univ_ISQDimensionBase {M : Type} [CommMonoid M] (f : ISQDimensionBase → M) :
    ∏ b, f b = f .length * f .mass * f .time * f .current * f .temperature
      * f .amount * f .luminousIntensity

declarations.name: SIUnitChoices
declarations.doc:
A **typed SI unit choice**: a typed unit at every ISQ base quantity. This is the
seven-slot, current-based sibling of the five-slot, charge-based `LTMCTUnitChoices`,
produced by the same basis-generic `UnitSystem` / `UnitMagnitudeCatalog` machinery.
declarations.statement: abbrev SIUnitChoices

declarations.name: SIUnitChoices.SI
declarations.doc: The coherent SI unit choice: metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole, candela.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def SI : SIUnitChoices

declarations.name: SIUnitChoices.dimScale
declarations.doc:
The dimension-scaling homomorphism over the ISQ basis, obtained *for free* from the
generic `UnitScale.dimScale` fold — no per-basis hand-rolling.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def dimScale (u1 u2 : SIUnitChoices) : Dimension ISQDimensionBase →* ℝ≥0

declarations.name: SIUnitChoices.dimScale_self
declarations.doc: A quantity of ISQ dimension does not rescale between a unit choice and itself.
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScale_self (u : SIUnitChoices) (d : Dimension ISQDimensionBase) :
    dimScale u u d = 1

modules.doc:
## Types which depend on dimensions

In addition to types which carry a dimension, we also have types whose elements
depend on a choice of a units. For example a function
`f : M1 → M2` between two types `M1` and `M2` which carry dimensions does not itself
carry a dimensions, but is dependent on a choice of units.

We define three versions
- `UnitDependent M` having a function `scaleUnit : LTMCTUnitChoices → LTMCTUnitChoices → M → M`
  subject to two conditions `scaleUnit_trans` and `scaleUnit_id`
- `LinearUnitDependent M` extends `UnitDependent M` with additional linearity conditions
  on `scaleUnit`.
- `ContinuousLinearUnitDependent M` extends `LinearUnitDependent M` with an additional
  continuity condition on `scaleUnit`.

sections.text:
### Instances of the type classes

We construct instance of the `UnitDependent`, `LinearUnitDependent` and
  `ContinuousLinearUnitDependent` type classes based on `CarriesDimension`
  and functions.
## Some type classes to help track dimensions

declarations.name: UnitDependent
declarations.doc:
A type carries the instance `UnitDependent M` if it depends on a choice of units.
This dependence is manifested in `scaleUnit u1 u2` which describes how elements of `M` change
under a scaling of units which would take `u1` to `u2`.

This type is used for functions, and propositions etc.
declarations.statement:
class UnitDependent (M : Type) where
  /-- `scaleUnit u1 u2` is the map transforming elements of `M` under a
    scaling of units which would take the unit `u1` to the unit `u2`. This is not
    to say that in `scaleUnit u1 u2 m` that `m` should be interpreted as being in the units `u1`,
    although this is often the case.
  -/
  scaleUnit : LTMCTUnitChoices → LTMCTUnitChoices → M → M
  scaleUnit_trans : ∀ u1 u2 u3 m, scaleUnit u2 u3 (scaleUnit u1 u2 m) = scaleUnit u1 u3 m
  scaleUnit_trans' : ∀ u1 u2 u3 m, scaleUnit u1 u2 (scaleUnit u2 u3 m) = scaleUnit u1 u3 m
  scaleUnit_id : ∀ u m, scaleUnit u u m = m

declarations.name: MulUnitDependent
declarations.doc:
A type `M` with an instance of `UnitDependent M` such that `scaleUnit u1 u2` is compatible
with the `MulAction ℝ≥0 M` instance on `M`.
declarations.statement:
class MulUnitDependent (M : Type) [MulAction ℝ≥0 M] extends
    UnitDependent M where
  scaleUnit_mul : ∀ u1 u2 (r : ℝ≥0) m,
    scaleUnit u1 u2 (r • m) = r • scaleUnit u1 u2 m

declarations.name: LinearUnitDependent
declarations.doc:
A type `M` with an instance of `UnitDependent M` such that `scaleUnit u1 u2` is compatible
with the `Module ℝ M` instance on `M`.
declarations.statement:
class LinearUnitDependent (M : Type) [AddCommMonoid M] [Module ℝ M] extends UnitDependent M where
  scaleUnit_add : ∀ u1 u2 m1 m2,
    scaleUnit u1 u2 (m1 + m2) = scaleUnit u1 u2 m1 + scaleUnit u1 u2 m2
  scaleUnit_smul : ∀ u1 u2 (r : ℝ) m,
    scaleUnit u1 u2 (r • m) = r • scaleUnit u1 u2 m

declarations.name: ContinuousLinearUnitDependent
declarations.doc:
A type `M` with an instance of `UnitDependent M` such that `scaleUnit u1 u2` is compatible
with the `Module ℝ M` instance on `M`, and is continuous.
declarations.statement:
class ContinuousLinearUnitDependent (M : Type) [AddCommMonoid M] [Module ℝ M]
    [TopologicalSpace M] extends LinearUnitDependent M where
  scaleUnit_cont : ∀ u1 u2, Continuous (scaleUnit u1 u2)

declarations.name: UnitDependent.scaleUnit_symm_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma UnitDependent.scaleUnit_symm_apply {M : Type} [UnitDependent M]
    (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (m : M) :
    scaleUnit u2 u1 (scaleUnit u1 u2 m) = m

declarations.name: UnitDependent.scaleUnit_injective
declarations.statement:
lemma UnitDependent.scaleUnit_injective {M : Type} [UnitDependent M]
    (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (m1 m2 : M) :
    scaleUnit u1 u2 m1 = scaleUnit u1 u2 m2 ↔ m1 = m2

declarations.name: UnitDependent.scaleUnitEquiv
declarations.doc: For an `M` with an instance of `UnitDependent M`, `scaleUnit u1 u2` as an equivalence.
declarations.statement:
def UnitDependent.scaleUnitEquiv {M : Type} [UnitDependent M]
    (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) : M ≃ M

declarations.name: LinearUnitDependent.scaleUnitLinear
declarations.doc:
For an `M` with an instance of `LinearUnitDependent M`, `scaleUnit u1 u2` as a
linear map.

def LinearUnitDependent.scaleUnitLinear
    {M : Type} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module ℝ M] [LinearUnitDependent M]
    (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) :
    M →ₗ[ℝ] M

declarations.name: LinearUnitDependent.scaleUnitLinearEquiv
declarations.doc:
For an `M` with an instance of `LinearUnitDependent M`, `scaleUnit u1 u2` as a
linear equivalence.
declarations.statement:
def LinearUnitDependent.scaleUnitLinearEquiv {M : Type} [AddCommMonoid M]

For an `M` with an instance of `ContinuousLinearUnitDependent M`, `scaleUnit u1 u2` as a

declarations.doc:
For an `M` with an instance of `ContinuousLinearUnitDependent M`, `scaleUnit u1 u2` as a
continuous linear equivalence.
declarations.statement:
def ContinuousLinearUnitDependent.scaleUnitContLinearEquiv {M : Type} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module ℝ M]
    [TopologicalSpace M] [ContinuousLinearUnitDependent M]
    (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) : M ≃L[ℝ] M

declarations.name: ContinuousLinearUnitDependent.scaleUnitContLinearEquiv_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma ContinuousLinearUnitDependent.scaleUnitContLinearEquiv_apply
    {M : Type} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℝ M] [TopologicalSpace M]
    [ContinuousLinearUnitDependent M]
    (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (m : M) :
    (ContinuousLinearUnitDependent.scaleUnitContLinearEquiv u1 u2) m =

declarations.statement:
lemma ContinuousLinearUnitDependent.scaleUnitContLinearEquiv_symm_apply
    {M : Type} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℝ M] [TopologicalSpace M]
    [ContinuousLinearUnitDependent M]
    (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (m : M) :
    (ContinuousLinearUnitDependent.scaleUnitContLinearEquiv u1 u2).symm m =

noncomputable instance : UnitDependent LTMCTUnitChoices

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.scaleUnit_apply_fst
declarations.statement:
lemma LTMCTUnitChoices.scaleUnit_apply_fst (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) :
    (scaleUnit u1 u2 u1) = u2

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_scaleUnit
LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScaleUnits_scaleUnit
Dimensionful.of_scaleUnit_units
declarations.statement:
lemma Dimensionful.of_scaleUnit_units {M : Type} [CarriesDimension M] {u1 u2 u : LTMCTUnitChoices}
    (c : Dimensionful M) :
    c.1 (scaleUnit u1 u2 u) =
    u1.dimScaleUnits u2 (dim M) • c.1 (u)
noncomputable instance {M1 : Type} [CarriesDimension M1] : UnitDependent M1

declarations.name: HasDim.scaleUnit_apply_units
declarations.statement:
lemma HasDim.scaleUnit_apply_units {M : Type} [CarriesDimension M]
    (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (m : M) :
    scaleUnit u1 u2 m = (u1.dimScaleUnits u2 (dim M)) • m

declarations.name: HasDim.scaleUnit_apply
declarations.doc:
The scaling of a type carrying a dimension which also has an action of `ℝ≥0`, phrased with
`dimScale` in place of `dimScaleUnits`.
declarations.statement:
lemma HasDim.scaleUnit_apply {M : Type} [HasDim M] [MulAction ℝ≥0 M]
    (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (m : M) :
    scaleUnit u1 u2 m = (u1.dimScale u2 (dim M)) • m

declarations.doc:
A type carrying a dimension which also has a `MulAction ℝ≥0` compatible with the scaling by
units is `MulUnitDependent`. A type whose elements are strictly positive carries no action of
`ℝ≥0` compatible with its magnitude, and so is `UnitDependent` only.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance {M1 : Type} [HasDim M1] [MulAction ℝ≥0 M1] : MulUnitDependent M1

noncomputable instance {M : Type} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module ℝ M] [HasDim M] :
    LinearUnitDependent M

noncomputable instance {M : Type} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module ℝ M]
    [HasDim M] [TopologicalSpace M]
    [ContinuousConstSMul ℝ M] : ContinuousLinearUnitDependent M

noncomputable instance {M1 M2 : Type} [UnitDependent M2] :
    UnitDependent (M1 → M2)

declarations.name: UnitDependent.scaleUnit_apply_fun_right
declarations.statement:

declarations.name: IsDimensionallyCorrect
declarations.doc:
A term of type `M` carrying an instance of `UnitDependent M` is said to be
dimensionally correct if under a change of units it remains the same.

More colloquially, something is dimensionally correct if it (e.g. it's value or its truth
for a proposition) does not depend on the units it is written in.

For the case of `m : M` with `CarriesDimension M` then `IsDimensionallyCorrect m`
corresponds to the statement that `m` does not depend on units, e.g. is zero
or the dimension of `M` is zero.
declarations.statement: def IsDimensionallyCorrect {M : Type} [UnitDependent M] (m : M) : Prop

modules.title: Unit systems, parametrised in a dimension basis
modules.doc:
A **unit system** is the everyday physics object: a rule fixing one concrete unit for
each base quantity. SI fixes the metre for length, the second for time, the kilogram for
mass, …; CGS fixes the centimetre, second and gram. Choosing a system gives every quantity
a numerical value; changing systems rescales those values.

This module makes that notion work for *any* dimension basis `B` (matching the
basis-generic `Dimension B`), while keeping units *typed*: the unit in the length slot has
type `LengthUnit`, the one in the time slot `TimeUnit`, so the checker rejects a mass unit
in a length slot.

* `UnitMagnitudeCatalog B` — the **menu** for basis `B`. For each base dimension `b : B` it
  gives a *type* `Unit b` of admissible units — so a dimension may offer many (length: metre,
  kilometre, micrometre, …) — and a *function* `mag` assigning each unit its one positive-real
  magnitude. The menu lists the options and picks none; many unit systems share one catalog.
* `UnitSystem B` — the **pick**: a function choosing *exactly one* unit per base dimension. A
  single unit system therefore fixes one length unit — metre *or* kilometre, never both — so
  metre and kilometre are two menu entries selected by two different `UnitSystem`s over the
  same catalog. SI and CGS are two such picks.
* `UnitSystem.toScale : UnitSystem B → UnitScale B` — forget the unit *types*, keep only
  the magnitudes, landing in the bare magnitude layer `UnitScale B` where the scaling
  homomorphism `UnitScale.dimScale` is proved once.

**Menu vs. pick.** The catalog is a menu, not a choice: it says which units exist and what
each weighs, but selects none — a `UnitSystem` makes the selection. And in PhysLib a base
unit *is* a positive real (`{ val : ℝ // 0 < val }`), i.e. its own magnitude, so the
magnitude comes fixed with the unit; there is no separate "assign a magnitude" step. Hence
metre, micrometre and kilometre are three *different* units on the one length menu, and
"SI in metres" versus "the same in micrometres" are two different `UnitSystem`s over the
**same** catalog — related by `UnitScale.dimScale`, which computes the 10⁶ factor between
them. (The multiplicity one might expect from "many magnitudes" lives here, among the unit
systems, not in many catalogs.)

The `LTMCTDimensionBase` catalog recovers PhysLib's five named unit types, and
`LTMCTUnitChoices ≃ UnitSystem LTMCTDimensionBase` exhibits the bespoke five-field record
as that instance. Scaling laws are **not** re-proved here — they live once on `UnitScale B`,
and the typed layer is a thin faithful wrapper projecting onto it via `toScale`.

This is the typed, basis-generic layer discussed as "Option D" in the review of the
dimension-parametrisation PR; it is the only design that keeps *both* basis-genericity and
typed-unit safety.

sections.text:
## The `LTMCTDimensionBase` catalog

The default basis's `UnitMagnitudeCatalog` recovers exactly PhysLib's five named typed unit
types, so `UnitSystem LTMCTDimensionBase` is the typed five-slot unit system and
`u .length : LengthUnit`, `LengthUnit.meters`, … all still work — and a `MassUnit` cannot
be placed in the length slot.

## `LTMCTUnitChoices` is `UnitSystem LTMCTDimensionBase`

The bespoke five-field record and the generic unit system over the default basis carry
the same data.

## The bespoke scaling law is the generic fold

`LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale` — the five explicit `rpow` factors written out by hand in
`Basic.lean` — is exactly the generic `UnitScale.dimScale` fold (a `Finset.prod` over the
basis) at the `LTMCTDimensionBase` instance, applied to `toScale`. This is what makes the
typed layer a *faithful* wrapper rather than a second, independent statement of the
scaling law: there is one source of truth, the generic fold on `UnitScale B`.

declarations.name: UnitMagnitudeCatalog
declarations.doc:
A **menu of typed units** for a basis `B`: for each base dimension `b : B`, a *type*
`Unit b` of admissible units (a dimension may offer several — metre, kilometre, …) and a
*function* `mag` giving each its single positive-real magnitude. It lists the options and
picks none — a `UnitSystem` makes the pick. One catalog underlies many unit systems (SI,
CGS, …); the magnitude is the data `toScale` reads to drive rescaling.
declarations.statement:
class UnitMagnitudeCatalog (B : Type) where
  /-- The typed unit type at each base dimension. -/
  Unit : B → Type
  /-- The positive-real magnitude of a typed unit. -/
  mag : {b : B} → Unit b → ℝ≥0
  /-- Every typed unit has a positive magnitude. -/
  mag_pos : ∀ {b : B} (u : Unit b), 0 < mag u

declarations.name: UnitSystem
declarations.doc:
A **unit system** over a basis `B` with a `UnitMagnitudeCatalog`: one typed unit chosen
per base dimension — the pick off the catalog's menu, and the formal counterpart of SI,
CGS, …. Over the default basis, `u .length : LengthUnit`, and a `MassUnit` cannot be
placed in the length slot.
declarations.statement: def UnitSystem (B : Type) [UnitMagnitudeCatalog B]

declarations.name: UnitSystem.ext
declarations.doc:
Two unit systems agree once they pick the same unit at every base dimension: `UnitSystem`
is extensional, as befits a choice-per-dimension.
declarations.statement: theorem ext {u v : UnitSystem B} (h : ∀ b, u b = v b) : u = v

declarations.name: UnitSystem.toScale
declarations.doc:
Forget a unit system to its magnitude layer `UnitScale B`: keep each chosen unit's
magnitude, drop its type — the layer where `UnitScale.dimScale` is already proved.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def toScale (u : UnitSystem B) : UnitScale B

declarations.name: UnitSystem.toScale_scale
declarations.statement:
lemma toScale_scale (u : UnitSystem B) (b : B) :
    (toScale u).scale b = UnitMagnitudeCatalog.mag (u b)
noncomputable instance : UnitMagnitudeCatalog LTMCTDimensionBase

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.equivUnitSystem
declarations.doc:
The bespoke five-field `LTMCTUnitChoices` and the generic `UnitSystem LTMCTDimensionBase`
are the same data.
declarations.statement: def equivUnitSystem : LTMCTUnitChoices ≃ UnitSystem LTMCTDimensionBase

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.toScale_equivUnitSystem
declarations.doc:
The typed generic projection agrees with the bespoke `LTMCTUnitChoices.toScale`: reading
`LTMCTUnitChoices` as a `UnitSystem` and forgetting to the magnitude layer is the same as
the bespoke `toScale`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toScale_equivUnitSystem (u : LTMCTUnitChoices) :
    (equivUnitSystem u).toScale = u.toScale

declarations.name: prod_univ_LTMCTDimensionBase
declarations.doc:
The product over the five default base quantities, in canonical enumeration order — a
reusable fact about the `Fintype` enumeration of `LTMCTDimensionBase`, for folding
`Finset.prod` over the default basis (e.g. in a hand-rolled scaling law).
declarations.statement:
lemma prod_univ_LTMCTDimensionBase {M : Type} [CommMonoid M]
    (f : LTMCTDimensionBase → M) :
    ∏ b, f b = f .length * f .time * f .mass * f .charge * f .temperature

declarations.name: LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale_eq_toScale_dimScale
declarations.doc:
The hand-rolled five-factor `LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale` equals the basis-generic
`UnitScale.dimScale` fold at `LTMCTDimensionBase`, applied to `toScale`. The scaling law
therefore has a single source of truth on the magnitude layer `UnitScale B`.
declarations.statement:
lemma dimScale_eq_toScale_dimScale (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase) :
    u1.dimScale u2 d = UnitScale.dimScale u1.toScale u2.toScale d

modules.title: A. Analysis of dimension-tagged quantities
modules.doc:
The numerical value of `WithDim d M` identifies it with `M`. We use that explicit
identification to induce a norm on the existing additive group, not to replace
its addition, natural/integer scalar multiplication, or the existing `NNReal` action.

The norm measures a numerical representation in fixed units. It is not asserted to
be invariant under a change of units. The coordinate equivalence is explicit: no
coercion silently discards a dimension tag. No `Ring` or `Field` on a nontrivial
physical dimension is introduced.

`transport` and `transportLinearMap` lift a function and its derivative between tagged
coordinates. They do not assert that the function is dimensionally correct. In particular,
changing the units of model parameters is a separate question. `hasFDerivAt_transport`
uses the existing calculus of continuous linear equivalences.

modules.doc:
## WithDim

WithDim is the type `M` which carrying the dimension `d`.

The dimension `d : Dimension B` may be taken over any basis `B` of base dimensions.
The *algebraic* structure of `WithDim d M` (its additive, order, scalar-action,
multiplication, division and casting instances) is available for every basis `B`.
The *unit-scaling* structure (`HasDim`, `DMul`, and the `scaleUnit` lemmas), which
routes through `LTMCTUnitChoices.dimScale`, is provided for the standard basis
`LTMCTDimensionBase`.

Real scalar multiplication acts on numerical values. Import
`Physlib.Units.WithDim.Analysis` for the normed-space structures and explicit
coordinate equivalences used to reuse existing analytic results.

declarations.doc: The type `M` carrying an instance of a dimension `d`.
declarations.statement:

  /-- The underlying value of `M`. -/

declarations.name: WithDim.smul_val
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_val {B : Type} [DimensionBasis B] {d : Dimension B} {M : Type} [MulAction ℝ≥0 M]
    (a : ℝ≥0) (m : WithDim d M) :
    (a • m).val = a • m.val

declarations.doc: The underlying value of a scaling by a unit of `ℝ≥0`, that is by a strictly positive real.

declarations.name: WithDim.ofPositiveRealUnit
declarations.doc:
A positive-real quantity which carries a dimension, regarded as a dimension-tagged real, so
that it can be used alongside the other dimension-tagged quantities. The dimension is read off
the `HasDim` instance, so the two cannot drift apart.
declarations.statement:
def ofPositiveRealUnit {U : Type} [PositiveRealUnitCore U] [HasDim U] (x : U) :
    WithDim (dim U) ℝ

declarations.name: WithDim.ofPositiveRealUnit_val
declarations.statement:
lemma ofPositiveRealUnit_val {U : Type} [PositiveRealUnitCore U] [HasDim U] (x : U) :
    (ofPositiveRealUnit x).val = PositiveRealUnitCore.val x

declarations.name: WithDim.ofPositiveRealUnit_units_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma ofPositiveRealUnit_units_smul {U : Type} [PositiveRealUnitCore U] [HasDim U]
    (a : ℝ≥0ˣ) (x : U) :
    ofPositiveRealUnit (a • x) = a • ofPositiveRealUnit x

declarations.name: WithDim.ofPositiveRealUnit_of_scaleUnit
declarations.doc:
A dimensionful positive-real quantity, such as the speed of light, may be tagged with its
dimension either before or after a change of units: `ofPositiveRealUnit` commutes with
`scaleUnit`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofPositiveRealUnit_of_scaleUnit {U : Type} [PositiveRealUnitCore U] [HasDim U]
    {u1 u2 u : LTMCTUnitChoices} (c : Dimensionful U) :
    ofPositiveRealUnit (c.1 (UnitDependent.scaleUnit u1 u2 u)) =
    UnitDependent.scaleUnit u1 u2 (ofPositiveRealUnit (c.1 u))

declarations.doc: Dimensionless real scalars act on the numerical value of a tagged quantity.
declarations.statement:

declarations.statement:
lemma scaleUnit_val_eq_scaleUnit_val {d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase} (M : Type) [MulAction ℝ≥0 M]
    (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (m1 m2 : WithDim d M) :
    (scaleUnit u1 u2 m1).val = (scaleUnit u1 u2 m2).val ↔ m1.val = m2.val

declarations.name: WithDim.scaleUnit_val_eq_scaleUnit_val_of_dim_eq
WithDim.scaleUnit_val
declarations.statement:
lemma scaleUnit_val {d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase} (M : Type) [MulAction ℝ≥0 M]
    (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (m1 : WithDim d M) :
    (scaleUnit u1 u2 m1).val = u1.dimScale u2 d • m1.val

declarations.name: WithDim.scaleUnit_val_pos
declarations.doc:
Scaling by a change of units preserves positivity of the value of a dimensionful
quantity.
declarations.statement:
lemma scaleUnit_val_pos {d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase} (m : WithDim d ℝ≥0) (hm : 0 < m.val)
    (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) : 0 < (scaleUnit u1 u2 m).val

declarations.name: WithDim.val_div_val
WithDim.div_scaleUnit
declarations.statement:
lemma div_scaleUnit {d1 d2 : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase} (m1 : WithDim d1 ℝ) (m2 : WithDim d2 ℝ)
    (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) :
    (scaleUnit u1 u2 m1) / (scaleUnit u1 u2 m2) = scaleUnit u1 u2 (m1 / m2)

declarations.name: WithDim.scaleUnit_dim_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma scaleUnit_dim_eq_zero {d : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase} (m : WithDim d ℝ)
    (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) (h : d = 1 := by ext <;> {simp; try ring}) :
    scaleUnit u1 u2 m = m

declarations.name: WithDim.cast
declarations.doc: The casting from `WithDim d M` to `WithDim d2 M` when `d = d2`.
declarations.statement:
def cast {B : Type} [DimensionBasis B] {d d2 : Dimension B} {M : Type} (m : WithDim d M)
    (h : d = d2 := by ext <;> {simp; try ring}) : WithDim d2 M

declarations.name: WithDim.cast_refl
declarations.statement:
lemma cast_refl {B : Type} [DimensionBasis B] {d : Dimension B} {M : Type} (m : WithDim d M) :
    cast m rfl = m

declarations.name: WithDim.cast_scaleUnit
declarations.statement:
lemma cast_scaleUnit {d d2 : Dimension LTMCTDimensionBase} {M : Type} [MulAction ℝ≥0 M]
    (m : WithDim d M)
    (h : d = d2) (u1 u2 : LTMCTUnitChoices) :
    cast (scaleUnit u1 u2 m) h = scaleUnit u1 u2 (cast m h)
